title: Speed up slow loops and algorithms
when: A script or function is slow on larger data, a loop takes seconds, or the page freezes while processing.
prompt:
Goal: Measured speedup by fixing the complexity first, with identical results.
Steps:
1. Measure before changing: performance.now() around the call with realistic data size; record the time.
2. Find nested work: a find, filter, includes or indexOf inside a loop makes it quadratic.
3. Build a Map or Set index once (byId = new Map(items.map(i => [i.id, i]))) and look up in constant time.
4. Avoid repeated work: hoist invariant calculations out of loops, sort once, cache results of pure functions by key.
5. Avoid building strings or arrays with repeated spreading in a loop; push then join.
6. Measure again with the same data and confirm the outputs match the old version.
Quality bar:
- The gain is measured, not assumed.
- The code stays readable.
- Results are identical on a sample set.
Pitfalls:
- Micro tuning syntax while an O(n squared) loop remains.
- Caching data that can change without invalidation.
- Optimizing code that runs once on ten items.
Verify:
- [ ] Before and after timings are written down.
- [ ] Outputs match for the sample data.
- [ ] No lookup inside a loop scans a whole array.
- [ ] Files parse.
Output: The optimized function and a short note: cause, change, timings.

examples.input: this report script takes 40 seconds for 50k rows
examples.output: replaced orders.find inside the loop with a Map index: 40 s to 0.3 s, same totals
